feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: it presents clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector specialization. It reads professionally and is largely error-free, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression at NACo, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director, which strengthens credibility.  
- Good use of scale and scope metrics (10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers), which improves impact.  
- Strong alignment between headline, competencies, experience, and technical skills; the profile feels focused and coherent.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across sections: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and readability.  
- Add more outcome-focused achievements beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and earlier positions; quantify business/user impact where possible.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: mixed punctuation in bullets, inconsistent use of “and” vs “&,” and title casing choices. Minor grammar/style points: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly—use “A2 (learning)”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler in Education.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector relevance. However, it is slightly broad and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the opening and foreground the most distinctive value: enterprise web modernization for complex public-sector organizations.
- Replace “Leads” with a first-person implied summary style that matches the rest of the CV more naturally.
- Add one concrete scale marker from recent experience to increase impact without overloading the intro.
- Simplify the service list so it reads as a focused executive profile, not a duplicate skills section.

Possible rewrite:
Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing web platforms, governance models, and content operations for high-volume public-sector organizations. Brings end-to-end leadership across enterprise website strategy, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production, and AI-enabled content experiences, including large-scale Drupal environments serving millions of annual page views.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences,” analytics, editorial systems, and multimedia production are repeated heavily in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.
- The subtitle already signals digital platform leadership, so avoid restating too many platform categories here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes that align well with the headline and recent roles, but this section overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be stronger if tightened, made more distinctive, and phrased more consistently.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: “Enterprise web modernization” instead of “Enterprise website modernization.”
- Replace broad items with more differentiated ones: “Cross-channel communications operations” or “Editorial workflow design and governance.”
- Consider a tighter version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial workflows • Analytics, dashboards and reporting infrastructure • Cross-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Keep “AI-enabled search” and “public-sector advocacy” because they are current and distinctive.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This block substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider trimming to 6 items or using it only if those sections are shortened.
- “Multimedia production and livestream operations” is also covered clearly in Topline Skills and work experience.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant examples that reinforce the CV’s themes, but the block is too dense and repeats several points already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or distinct scope will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a clean list format and parallel structure: project name + action + distinguishing result/purpose.
- Replace generic phrasing like “built”/“developed” with more specific verbs such as “launched,” “architected,” or “produced.”
- Shorten descriptions and foreground the most relevant elements: AI search, Drupal 10 microsite, interactive campaign, recurring video program.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “10 x 20-foot,” and consistent comma usage throughout.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current freelance and NACo experience bullets.
- Consider framing these as selected examples with unique implementation details, not restatements of role responsibilities.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope and technical depth, but it reads as a task list. Tighten the phrasing and foreground outcomes, especially where this role extends beyond your NACo experience rather than repeating it.

Suggested edit:
- Open with impact + client context: “Lead digital strategy, platform improvement and content operations for a U.S. national membership organization, strengthening enterprise communications across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Replace generic verbs with sharper ones: “Designed and implemented” instead of “build and refine”; “Developed” or “launched” instead of “support.”
- Consolidate overlapping platform bullets into 2 stronger bullets, e.g.:
- “Designed Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved enterprise web operations through CMS/front-end implementation, analytics workflows, governance guidance and technical troubleshooting.”
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search success, engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics, enterprise web improvement” overlaps heavily with the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize consulting ownership, AI search, or campaign builds.
- The Drupal microsite and AI search bullets duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level if those projects stay in the footer.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and the bullets emphasized outcomes, team scope, and transformation over channel ownership.

Suggested edit
- Replace the first sentence with a tighter leadership summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national association.”
- Tighten and front-load impact in bullets: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable outcomes where missing: email/social growth, reporting efficiency, production cost/time savings from the studio, governance adoption, or workflow improvements.
- Use stronger result language: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing advocacy and event production capacity” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery to improve executive reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language may duplicate older NACo roles; emphasize building the studio and scaling capacity here.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director of Digital Media role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership and channel growth before the higher-level strategy/governance promotion.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, scaling editorial operations and advocacy messaging for a national public-sector membership audience.”
- Tighten bullets and emphasize ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and stakeholders.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, video views, audience growth, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of cross-team contributors coordinated.
- Replace weaker phrasing like “helped improve” with direct action: “Standardized digital publishing workflows, improving consistency, speed and cross-team coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/coordination” and “improved publishing workflows” overlap with the Director role’s governance/planning bullets.
- “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update” is close to the earlier role’s “weekly video updates”; distinguish by scale or ownership.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo/consulting bullets. Make it sharper and more senior by emphasizing enterprise scope, governance, and audience outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy & information architecture
- If space allows, swap “content planning” for “information architecture” or “content operations” to better reflect recent Drupal/governance work.
- Keep terms aligned with strongest recent evidence: enterprise web improvement, governance, analytics-informed operations, and campaign/storytelling experiences.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is supported, but “audience-focused content planning” feels weaker and vaguer than your recent experience suggests.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, make it more outcome-oriented and emphasize the platforms/technical strengths most supported by recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, higher-value phrases rather than a raw list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint, WordPress, and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most validated by recent experience.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based systems” and “AI-enabled search experiences” with “AI-enabled search and content discovery” for cleaner phrasing.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web platforms” to signal scale.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and let the detailed tools live there.
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies and Technical + IT.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack for recent leadership roles, but the item reads like a raw keyword list. It would be stronger if framed around business use—measurement, reporting, and optimization—and trimmed to avoid overlap with broader “Data analytics & reporting” language elsewhere.

Suggested edit
- Recast from tools-only to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, KPI design, executive reporting, and digital performance optimization”
- Group tools more cleanly: “GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with a sharper term like “Executive dashboards” or “Executive reporting”
- Consider a tighter final version: “Analytics strategy & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, KPI design, executive dashboards, SEO/performance analysis”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Data analytics & reporting” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating that exact phrasing here.
- This skill line closely mirrors the NACo Director bullet on analytics infrastructure, so keep this section concise and let the work experience carry the proof.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skills item is relevant, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and technical depth rather than broad labels.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe for specificity: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera operation/systems • Studio buildout and operations • Virtual event production”
- If accurate, strengthen with scale/quality cues: add terms like “broadcast-quality,” “multi-camera,” or “end-to-end” to reflect the in-house studio achievement.
- Keep phrasing parallel and concise; avoid mixing nouns and gerunds. For example, use all noun phrases rather than “Video production and editing” + “Livestreaming.”
- Consider replacing “Hybrid and virtual event production” with “Hybrid, virtual, and livestream event delivery” to reduce repetition and sharpen execution focus.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production.”
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the NACo studio bullet; don’t repeat that accomplishment elsewhere verbatim.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent experience is strongest in Drupal-led modernization, this item should emphasize depth/order and trim lower-value entries.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling strength: “Drupal (enterprise migration, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If formatting allows, add proficiency context rather than just names, especially for Drupal given the 10,000+ page migration and current consulting work.
- Consider dropping GitHub Pages unless it supports a meaningful recent project; it feels lighter than the rest and may dilute enterprise credibility.
- Keep this item concise and let work experience carry outcomes; don’t try to force metrics into the skills list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Consider merging or differentiating one as “Platforms” and the other as “Technical capabilities.”
- “Web & CMS administration” already appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the same framing here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Make it more current and implementation-focused by emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles and trimming older/basic items.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show applied capability, not just languages: “Front-end implementation: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Group modern tooling separately: “Technical tooling: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Drop version numbers unless required: use “HTML, CSS” instead of “HTML5, CSS3”
- If accurate, add one higher-value qualifier tied to recent work, e.g. “custom Drupal front-end implementation” or “deployment/workflow automation”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills; consider removing those from one section.
- “GitHub Actions” may overlap with “Workflow automation” unless you distinguish it as deployment/CI tooling.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a pure list to grouped, capability-led phrasing: “Workflow automation & work management: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier; project operations: Jira, Asana, Basecamp, Trello; collaboration: Slack, Teams.”
- If space allows, add a light outcomes cue tied to recent work, e.g. “used to streamline editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and communications operations.”
- Prioritize the strongest/recently relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana; consider dropping one or two lower-value collaboration tools.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; “Microsoft Teams” may read stronger than “Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear under Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same language here.
- Slack/Teams are generic collaboration tools and may add little unless other lower-priority tools are removed.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This is clear but too bare compared with the rest of the CV. Since email is a major theme in recent roles, this line should signal platform depth and audience engagement use cases, not just list tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Rewrite as: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope/context: Used for newsletter operations, campaign journeys, member communications, and audience segmentation
- If space allows, strengthen with level of use: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter production)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/newsletter leadership is already covered strongly in NACo roles; avoid repeating outcomes here unless you add platform-specific detail.
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader multi-channel claims elsewhere; keep this item focused on systems/platforms.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization” and uses a few generic terms. Tighten it to emphasize platforms and methods, and reserve outcomes for recent experience bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI reporting
- Swap “SEO” for “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to make the skill more concrete and tool/method specific.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for clearer business value.
- If space allows elsewhere, connect these tools to impact in recent roles, e.g., “Expanded analytics infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery to improve leadership reporting and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item is nearly identical to Topline Skills [3]; consider deleting one or making this version more tool-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating explanatory phrasing here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating website/video points already covered above.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add scope or output metrics if available: website traffic, livestream/event volume, video cadence, email list size, or turnaround improvements.
- Make contributions more direct and concise: “Supported a major website refresh; produced livestreams and weekly video updates; coached a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- If possible, include one outcome: improved production capacity, faster publishing, stronger audience engagement, or reduced reliance on vendors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this as launching or piloting the format.
- “Website refresh” may feel repetitive next to the later full Drupal redesign unless you clarify it was an earlier refresh, not the major migration.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production” with a more active, specific verb: “produced” or “developed multimedia and digital content assets.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/programs served.
- Keep this entry to 1–2 lines since later roles show broader digital leadership and execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/digital roles; avoid repeating broad media language unless tied to the podcast.
- “Supporting organizational programs and policy work” is generic; use only if you can specify initiative type or stakeholder group.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it reads as a mixed list of software, workflows, and production capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to emphasize tools only or rename it to reflect both tools and production.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: “Creative Tools & Production” or keep “Multimedia Tools” if you want a cleaner software-focused category.
